Holy Ten Rape Case Postponed To November 5 As Investigations Continue

Holy Ten Rape Case Postponed To November 5 As Police Finalise Investigations

Rapper Mukudzei Chitsama, popularly known as Holy Ten, will return to court on November 5 after his rape case involving a 14-year-old girl was postponed.

The musician appeared in court today, where the matter was deferred pending the finalisation of investigations into the allegations against him, ZBC reveals.

Also Read: Holy Ten Arrested Over Alleged Rape Of 14-Year-Old Girl

How Holy Ten Allegedly Met The Teenager

Holy Ten was arrested in July 2026 over allegations that he raped the teenager.

According to sources familiar with the case, the girl first made contact with the rapper through social media while she was staying in South Africa. She had recently returned to Zimbabwe when she arranged to meet him.

The teenager reportedly travelled to Avondale on a Monday afternoon, accompanied by a friend, to meet Holy Ten at a music recording session.

The two allegedly waited for the musician to finish recording before the friend left for home, leaving the teenager with him.

Also Read: New Details Emerge in Holy Ten Alleged Rape Case

Alleged Incident At Hatfield House

Sources allege that Holy Ten subsequently took the girl to his home in Hatfield, telling her they would record videos.

Once inside the house, he allegedly led her into a bedroom and locked the door. Other people were reportedly present at the property but were in separate rooms.

The rapper is accused of raping the teenager without protection and threatening to kill her if she resisted.

These allegations have not been established in court.

Teenager Reportedly Told Her Aunt

After the alleged incident, Holy Ten reportedly arranged a taxi for the girl to return home.

Upon arriving, she allegedly told her aunt what had happened, leading to the matter being reported and the musician’s subsequent arrest in July.
